title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: connect agents to the remote Work IQ MCP server
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, delegated access, consumption licensing and governance controls are supported. Minor corrections would finish two navigation paths, cite the Copilot Studio integration and acknowledge that the consent checklist has no corresponding controls row.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap lists only Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The roadmap lists the Developer platform.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Developer"]

claims.claim: The roadmap target is June CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "June CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap describes remote MCP connections through the Work IQ endpoint for tools and services beyond the local runtime.
claims.quote: Supports connecting to remote MCP servers through the Work IQ endpoint, enabling agents to securely invoke external tools and services beyond the local runtime for richer, distributed agent orchestration.

claims.claim: The roadmap description does not identify a particular remote server.
claims.quote: Supports connecting to remote MCP servers through the Work IQ endpoint

claims.claim: Work IQ supports Remote MCP, Local MCP, A2A and REST protocols.
claims.quote: Work IQ supports the following protocols: ... A2A ... Local MCP ... Remote MCP ... REST

claims.claim: Remote MCP exposes Microsoft 365 work context as tools for AI assistants in developer environments.
claims.quote: Use remote MCP to expose Microsoft 365 work context as tools for AI assistants running in developer environments.

claims.claim: The remote Work IQ MCP endpoint is https://workiq.svc.cloud.microsoft/mcp.
claims.quote: Access to the remote Work IQ MCP server endpoint, `https://workiq.svc.cloud.microsoft/mcp`.

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP server provides its capabilities through a single MCP endpoint.
claims.quote: retrieve grounding content, and discover API schemas and connected Copilot Connector tools, all through a single MCP endpoint.

claims.claim: Generic Work IQ MCP tools operate on resource paths.
claims.quote: Tools work with relative resource paths. The path shows the resource, and the tool acts as the verb:

claims.claim: The listed entity tools are fetch, create_entity, update_entity, delete_entity, do_action and call_function.
claims.quote: Entity tools | `fetch`, `fetch_blob`, `create_entity`, `update_entity`, `delete_entity`, `do_action`, `call_function`

claims.claim: The Copilot tools are ask, retrieve and list_agents.
claims.quote: Copilot tools | `ask`, `retrieve`, `list_agents`

claims.claim: The schema tools are get_schema and search_paths.
claims.quote: Schema tools | `get_schema`, `search_paths`

claims.claim: The server supports reading and modifying entities across Microsoft 365 and connected enterprise systems.
claims.quote: It provides tools that enable agents to read, create, update, and delete entities across Microsoft 365 and connected enterprise systems

claims.claim: The retrieve tool is in public preview.
claims.quote: The `retrieve` tool is available in public preview.

claims.claim: Work IQ uses Microsoft Entra ID delegated authentication.
claims.quote: Work IQ uses Microsoft Entra ID delegated authentication.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Requests run in the signed-in user's context.
claims.quote: Requests run in the context of the signed-in user.

claims.claim: Application-only authentication is unsupported, so an application identity alone cannot run these requests.
claims.quote: Application-only authentication isn't supported.

claims.claim: The cited partner announcement is dated 3 June 2026.
claims.quote: Work IQ API and consumptive pricing update ... Date: June 3, 2026

claims.claim: The partner announcement gives 16 June 2026 as general availability for Work IQ API as a whole.
claims.quote: Work IQ API reaches GA June 16 with consumption-based pricing using Copilot Credits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ API has a consumption-based model using Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: The June announcement says there is no separate Work IQ API subscription, SKU or per-user licence.
claims.quote: There's no separate Work IQ API subscription, SKU, or per-user license.

claims.claim: Work IQ API is licensed under the agreement governing Microsoft Online Services.
claims.quote: Work IQ API is licensed under your agreement governing use of Microsoft Online Services, including the Microsoft Product Terms.

claims.claim: The June announcement says Work IQ use by Microsoft 365 Copilot prebuilt agents is covered by licensing without Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: For users accessing Microsoft 365 Copilot prebuilt agents, Work IQ usage is covered by licensing, and no Copilot Credits are required.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: Use requires administrator enablement, supporting admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: Before Work IQ usage can begin at GA on June 16, an administrator must enable consumptive billing.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Each documented Work IQ delegated permission requires administrator consent.
claims.quote: WorkIQAgent.Ask ... AdminConsentRequired | - | Yes ... WorkIQ.Act ... AdminConsentRequired | - | Yes ... WorkIQ.Read ... AdminConsentRequired | - | Yes

claims.claim: WorkIQAgent.Ask includes read and write access to Microsoft 365 resources accessible to Work IQ agents and scoped to the signed-in user.
claims.quote: This includes read and write access to Microsoft 365 resources that are accessible to Work IQ agents and scoped to the signed-in user.

claims.claim: fetch /me/messages is a documented mail-reading example.
claims.quote: fetch /me/messages                         → read my emails

claims.claim: fetch /me/chats/{id}/messages is a documented Teams chat-reading example.
claims.quote: fetch /me/chats/{id}/messages              → read Teams chat messages

claims.claim: call_function /search/query is a documented semantic-search example.
claims.quote: call_function /search/query                → semantic search

claims.claim: do_action /me/sendMail is a documented email-sending example.
claims.quote: do_action /me/sendMail                     → send an email

claims.claim: create_entity /me/events is a documented calendar-event creation example.
claims.quote: create_entity /me/events                   → create a calendar event

claims.claim: Allowed and blocked paths depend on per-tenant policy configuration.
claims.quote: The complete list of allowed and blocked paths depends on per-tenant policy configuration and might vary.

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP policy layer evaluates individual MCP requests at request time.
claims.quote: It adds a request-time governance layer that can allow or deny specific MCP tool requests based on tenant policy.

claims.claim: Policy complements rather than replaces authentication, OAuth permissions and user permissions.
claims.quote: policy governance doesn't replace Microsoft Entra authentication, OAuth permissions, or the signed-in user's existing Microsoft 365 permissions.

claims.claim: Policy cannot grant access beyond the signed-in user's existing access.
claims.quote: Policy can't grant access beyond what the signed-in user is already allowed to access.

claims.claim: The MCP tenant policy blocks mutation operations by default, including create, update, delete and data-modifying actions.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.

claims.claim: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center when those capabilities are needed.

claims.claim: Initial Work IQ MCP policy control is tenant-level.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control.

claims.claim: Per-user, per-app and per-agent policy templates are not part of the initial policy surface.
claims.quote: Per-user, per-app, per-agent, or scenario-specific policy templates aren't part of the initial policy control surface.

claims.claim: Policy changes can take up to 24 hours to apply.
claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.claim: The Work IQ service principal is created automatically on first use.
claims.quote: The Work IQ service principal is created automatically in the tenant when you use Work IQ for the first time.

claims.claim: Policy configuration before first MCP use can fail because the service principal does not yet exist.
claims.quote: such as configuring Work IQ MCP policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center before any MCP use in the tenant, the service principal might not exist yet and policy configuration can fail.

claims.claim: Tenant enablement lists Global Administrator for one-time Work IQ setup.
claims.quote: A user with Global Administrator role for the one-time Work IQ setup

claims.claim: The enablement prerequisites list a usage-based billing plan with an assigned Azure subscription.
claims.quote: A usage-based billing plan set up in Copilot Studio with an Azure subscription and resource group assigned.

claims.claim: The enablement prerequisites list an assigned resource group.
claims.quote: with an Azure subscription and resource group assigned.

claims.claim: The enablement prerequisites list a user assigned to the billing plan.
claims.quote: The user assigned to the billing plan

claims.claim: The tenant-enablement procedure can manually create the Work IQ service principal.
claims.quote: This section creates the Work IQ service principal in your organization, which provisions the Work IQ resource so your applications can request tokens for it.

claims.claim: The AI experience access page lists AI Administrator for Microsoft 365 admin center settings.
claims.quote: AI Administrator role to work with settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Block blocks the entire server, separately from Copilot audience settings and App Access.
claims.quote: This control applies to the entire Work IQ MCP server, separate from Copilot audience settings or App Access. ... Select Agents > Tools. ... Select Work IQ MCP. ... To block access to the server, select Block.

claims.claim: No documented Graph or PowerShell operation was found for the Work IQ MCP Block control, including applicability of copilotPackage: block.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP server block Microsoft Graph PowerShell tenant availability API. Opened manage-ai-experience-access, copilotpackage-block and Agent 365 manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers; package blocking is distinct from server blocking.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy reaches the tenant policy on/off setting.
claims.quote: select Agents > Tools. ... select Work IQ MCP. ... select the Policy tab when it's available. ... Review the current policy state, then turn policy on or off for the tenant as needed.
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path and the rendered path to 'Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy > policy on/off'; the cited page describes the final toggle without naming a more specific label.

claims.claim: No named Graph or PowerShell operation was found to change Work IQ MCP tenant policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP tenant policy Graph PowerShell API block server Allowed Disallowed policy settings; "Work IQ" "policy" "Graph" "update". Opened policy-governance-mcp and read returned Work IQ references; no policy-update operation was named.

claims.claim: Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > spending policy reaches the spending-policy settings fly-out in Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Cost Management. ... Select the Configuration tab. ... Select the spending policy you want to edit. ... This includes: ... Billing method ... Spending limits
claims.fix: Extend controls[2].ui.path and its rendered path to 'Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > spending policy > Spending limits or Billing method', matching the two settings already named in the note.

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} updates a spending policy.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/3f9e2c1a-0000-0000-0000-00000000c21b

claims.claim: The update request supports periodLimit, perUserLimit and billingMethods.
claims.quote: The following properties can be updated: `displayName`, `periodLimit`, `perUserLimit`, and `billingMethods`.

claims.claim: The spending-policy update uses delegated CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All permission.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All

claims.claim: The spending-policy Graph operation is a beta API.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Foundry's Work IQ API route through A2A, REST or MCP uses usage-based billing rather than connector licensing.
claims.quote: Work IQ API through A2A, REST, or MCP | Usage-based billing | Enable billing with Copilot Credits. This path doesn't use connector licensing.

claims.claim: Connector-backed Microsoft 365 tools can require a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence for each calling user.
claims.quote: Connector-backed Microsoft 365 tools | Connector licensing | Confirm the selected connector's prerequisites. A connector can require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license for each calling user.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter and controls
claims.claim: Work IQ API can consume the same shared tenant pool of Copilot Credits as Cowork and Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: Copilot Cowork, Copilot Studio agents, and Work IQ API can consume Copilot credits from a shared tenant pool.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter and controls
claims.claim: Spending policies control access and spending limits without reserving credits for workloads.
claims.quote: Spending policies control access and spending limits; they don't reserve or allocate credits for a workload, user, or group.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ API is a service managed through Copilot > Cost management and spending policies.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft admin center, Copilot > Cost management, admins can monitor Copilot Credit consumption and manage spending associated with the supported services such as ... Work IQ API.

claims.where: Scope: Users and licences; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The retrieve prerequisites require calling users to be assigned to a spending policy that includes Work IQ API.
claims.quote: Set up usage-based billing for Copilot Credits and assign the calling users to a spending policy that includes Work IQ API.

claims.claim: Spending policies provide policy-level and per-user monthly consumption limits.
claims.quote: When you select a limited monthly budget, you limit the number of credits that this policy can spend each month. ... Specify the maximum credit limit users can spend per month.

claims.claim: Cost management consumption can be reviewed by spending policy, user, group and service.
claims.quote: The Consumption tab enables detailed analysis by spending policy, user, group, agent, or service.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Documented 403 causes include missing consent, missing spending-policy coverage, exhausted limits, user access issues and policy denials.
claims.quote: `403 Forbidden` or access denied | Missing consent, no spending-policy coverage, exhausted limit, user access issue, or policy denial

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn's rollback guidance removes Work IQ API or a cohort from its policy to stop cohort usage, subject to reviewing other applicable policies including the default.
claims.quote: To stop Work IQ usage for only the migration cohort, remove Work IQ API from that cohort's spending policy or remove the cohort from the policy.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Excluding Work IQ API from one policy does not exclude it from other policies, so all applicable policies including the default must be reviewed.
claims.quote: Review all applicable policies, including the default policy. Excluding a service from one policy doesn't exclude it from other policies.

claims.claim: Work IQ integrations include coding assistants, Copilot Studio agents and Foundry agents.
claims.quote: Work IQ is generally available in Microsoft Copilot Studio and is added by default to every new agent that uses the Microsoft Copilot harness.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/add-work-iq to sources for the Copilot Studio integration; the existing GitHub Copilot CLI and Foundry sources support the other named clients.

claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to grant client-app consent, but the controls table has no consent row.
claims.quote: Grant admin consent only to named client applications ... Admin consent for the Work IQ permissions is a separate step that is not a row here.
claims.fix: The Before rollout consent-review step and At rollout 'Grant admin consent only to named client applications' step have no corresponding row in the controls table.

claims.claim: The variable cost rating reflects metered Work IQ API consumption in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Not yet published; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The cited billing overview publishes no credit rate per Work IQ MCP call.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP tool call Copilot Credits rate pricing licensing guide. Read usage-based-billing-overview-copilot-credits, api-overview, plugins/cost-considerations and June announcements; the overview names Work IQ API but gives no per-call credit rate.

claims.claim: The cited policy documentation does not state whether the policy on/off control is initially on.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP policy default on enabled first use existing users behavior. Read policy-governance-mcp, mcp/overview and tool-reference; mutation defaults are stated, but the initial on/off state of the tenant policy switch is not.

claims.claim: The policy page does not name the exact setting that enables supported mutation scenarios.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP tenant policy Graph PowerShell API block server Allowed Disallowed policy settings. Read policy-governance-mcp: it says admins can enable supported mutations through tenant policy but supplies no mutation-setting label.

claims.claim: No checked source states that this capability changes existing behaviour for users who do nothing.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP policy default on enabled first use existing users behavior. Read roadmap, API and MCP overviews, enable-work-iq and June announcements; no automatic change to inactive users is stated, and use requires billing enablement.

claims.claim: Learn documents connected-source tool paths through Work IQ.
claims.quote: For connected data sources, connector paths use `call_function` for reads and `do_action` for writes, rather than `fetch`, `create_entity`, `update_entity`, or `delete_entity`.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and At rollout
claims.claim: Spending policies let administrators select covered services and users or groups.
claims.quote: Select the agents and services that users and groups in this policy can access. ... At this time, you can only support specific users and resource accounts through security groups.

claims.claim: Block and tenant policy are separate controls for Work IQ MCP.
claims.quote: On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available. ... Review the current policy state, then turn policy on or off for the tenant as needed.

claims.claim: Work IQ can reason over files in OneDrive and SharePoint.
claims.quote: Documents in OneDrive and SharePoint
